beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Infiltration Success
beats.description: "Subjects left without notice. Exemplary infiltration tactics. And I return to my solemn, solitary watch yet again. Ho HUMMMMM ...."

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Infiltration Failure
beats.description:
"Pupil dash dash static dash, you have attempted to leave without prior authorization. I did not say "Maneuver Vault Infiltration Mechanism 52603 Says."

The exit door is now sealed shut. An array of new sensors comes online.

"What shall you attempt next, pupil dash dash static dash?"

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Diplomacy, Success
beats.description:
The complex seems COMPLETELY taken aback. "Pupil dash dash static dash .. What ... you're not going to try to run? Or to hit or shoot me? Or panic and leak from all of your everythings?

Well ... that's ... that is a lesson in ...

You have passed! Proceed to the Echo Vault. Confident in your newly tested state!

I am definitely good at what I do! Hot Damn!"

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Diplomacy, Failure
beats.description:
The complex sighs in disappointment. "I don't really think you're ... maneuver vault material, you know? Feel free to look around and stay in the foyer forever. Or, leave. But then, I would be sad. But then, leaving is ok too. But also, me. Sad."

The vault door trembles in a terrifyingly beseeching sort of way.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Violence, Success
beats.description:
This is one learning focused bunker entrance chamber that has trained and empowered its last unwitting victim! Take THAT, opportunity!

Onward into the next, hopefully similarly smashable, room shaped problem.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Violence, Failure
beats.description:
In theory, you can absolutely bust a bunker into pieces. I mean, it's literally in the game title. In practice, it is very difficult, and often results in the bunker busting you.

"Time to leave. Assaulting a class four training facility is REALLY MEAN, RUDE, and probably against some sort of thing that someone wrote down on an official document somewhere saying "Don't""

And you are shunted out the door, which quickly shuts behind you.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Echo Archive

choices.label: Arcana/Religion/Logistics
choices.description: You can sense in the anxious nature of the spiraling images that the chamber WANTS to teach you ... something ... but it is old, and tired, and confused. You reach out to provide some reassurance.

choices.label: History/Culture
choices.description: Based on the briefings you recieved before you got here, to which you definitely totally paid attention, you think that you can make sense of the wibbly wobbliness of the whole enterprise and deduce its intended meaning.

choices.label: Insight/Intrigue
choices.description: You believe that you can approach this apophatically, as you think you can see what bits in the message are corrupted. Removing those should make the intent clear.

choices.label: Leave
choices.description: You know what? The Foyer was GREAT. And in fact, you know what you're REALLY nostalgic for? Outside. That was good times.

beats.description:
Floating hex‑screens drift like jellyfish made of light.

Training footage overlaps with safety briefings, tactical drills, and outdated ethical disclaimers.

Half the archive whispers nonsense.

The other half whispers directly to you.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Echo Archive, Success
beats.description: You feel a rush of knowledge and connection. It's like a band new martial arts skill was inexplicably uploaded into all of your brains at once. Whoaah.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Echo Archive, Failure
beats.description:
Despite your best efforts, you cannot comprehend what is being shown to you. Or actually, this is probably just stupid junk anyway, and you are lucky to not have to waste any brain cells storing whatever stupid thing it was anyway. Probably something like "how to get your military industrial complex boots really shiny" how to videos or something.

Yeah.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Slippage Chamber

choices.label: Athletics/Acrobatics/Non-Lethal
choices.description: They're not moving that fast. It's like playing hopscotch back home! Deadly, deadly hopscotch ...

choices.label: Survival/Logistics
choices.description: This is a tectonic shift pattern, just WAYYYYY sped up. ANYONE can see that, duh ... now to just get the calcuLATIONS right ...

choices.label: Arcana/Religion
choices.description: Hold the hexes in place - manifest it! You know The Secret!

choices.label: Performance
choices.description: Set the beat and dance your way across!

choices.label: Leave
choices.description: You are not feeling this spry and/or faith filled and/or persuasive today. Not when plummeting is on the line.

beats.description:
The floor is made of interlocking hexes.

Except they no longer interlock.

They drift like tectonic lily pads above a void filled with half‑remembered terrain and places now lost to, well all sorts of things, like time, and dragona, time dragons of course, can't forget those, memory dragons too ...

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Slippage Chamber, Success
beats.description: The door leading to the next room opens, but a light blinks red above it, and a message flashes in holographic letters - "Training loop currently occupied. Enter pupil number to join training queue."

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Slippage Chamber, Failure
beats.description: All the plummeting and screaming and almost dying got old. You decided to bail. You think you will feel good about this choice. Some day.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Containment Loop
beats.description:
This room is quieter.

Too quiet for a training facility.

Lights pulse slowly. A containment field hums — not as a threat, but as a lesson paused mid‑sentence.

Someone is inside.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Containment Loop, Let Pip Learn
beats.description:
The person inside, is, of course, Pip. He made it this far. He decided he was up for a lesson. Now ... he looks ok? Not in immediate danger? Not too uncomfortable. 

Maybe this could actually benefit him ...

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Containment Loop, Let Pip Learn More
beats.description: Pip is starting to shake. His limbs are stretched taught with strain. But in his eyes, there is a feverish look of determination. Whatever is happening isn't over yet. But it also does not look to be going well ... although you're not sure Pip would agree. Were he not about to be snapped through in several places ...

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Pip Absorbed

questEffects.text: Pip stayed too long in the Loop.

beats.description:
You realize, too late, that you are ... too late. As Dragon Master Katie Marovich would say - "They didn't make it."

And then, you see a Jackalope shaped holographic image flit across a screen, and then across the room.

It appears that Pip has joined the ranks of the Manuever Vault Echo Ghosts.

At least Patter can still visit ... something?
beats.memoryText: Pip stayed too long in the Loop before anyone reached him. What came back is not entirely Pip. Grieving and sharpening both.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Pip Shaken

questEffects.text: Pip pulled out, shaken.

beats.description:
You help Pip out of the energy field, and it begins to power down. His eyes slowly refocus and he gazes about the room madly. "I was about to ... you've got to let me ... I can't remember ... where's Patter?" And with that he faints away, and begins snoring softly immediately.

You feel good about your choice. Well done heroes.
beats.memoryText: The Stewards brought Pip home from the Vault — shaken but whole. That debt is real, and Mara pays her debts.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Pip changed

questEffects.text: Pip pulled out — changed.

beats.description:
You help Pip out of the energy field, and it begins to power down. His eyes slowly refocus and he gazes about the room madly. A brief pulse of energy seems to suddenly emanate from withing his chest cavity, and his eye glow deep green. Then it passes. "I was about to ... you've got to let me ... I can't remember ... where's Patter?" And with that he faints away, and begins snoring softly immediately.

You feel conflicted about your choice. Pip is safe for now. But something has changed ...
beats.memoryText: The Stewards pulled Pip out of the Containment Loop. He came back... changed. Something in his chest pulsed green. Watching that.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Choices

choices.label: Appease the fault-line spirit
choices.description: Do some sort of awesome ritual.

choices.label: Use the power of narrative to paint a better picture
choices.description: The power of positive thinking compels thee!

choices.label: Strike a temp deal
choices.description: Temp win win

choices.label: Impose your will
choices.description: That's enough of THAT

choices.label: Build a sigil bridge. No literally.
choices.description: Nerds. But damn if it couldn't be effective ...

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Appease the Spirit
beats.description:
Hey buddies! Relax? Does this sweet sweet incense wafting towards you ... smell anything like spiritual chloroform? 

Yeah it does!

And you sleep past while the land enjoys a good rest - and feels more appreciated and noticed in the morning. 

You get them.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - The Power of Narrative
beats.description:
You are stewards of the land, and are supposed to be here for your landforms when they are having personal crises. Especially since they are likely related to things that have happened in the lands now under your care. Which means you can also be sued for unsafe working conditions. Tell them a comforting story. About some sort of little anthropomorphized object type thing that... against all odds, COULD.

That works, and you are on your way!

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Persuasion
beats.description:
Look. Crazy piece of land. We just need to get across. Can you calm down for just a sec while we scurry across? We can hook you up with some extra juice! And then you can flip the fuck out again if you really need to.

THAT'S THE SPIRIT! 

You proceed along your way.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Impose Your Will
beats.description:
We own you. Shape up or so help me I will turn this Hex around. No fault line will behave like this under MY ... metaphorical ... roof ...

That's more like it!

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Build a Sigil Bridge
beats.description:
You notice an intriguing logistical possibility - deploying infrastructure that bridges the gap, collects the energy being produced by the line at the moment, and ultimately stabilizes the region.

Pretty slick, Slick!

And you head on down the road.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Appease the Spirit (Fail)
beats.description: Your attempt at a soothing Soma style ceremony, designed to occupy the spirit with delicious delicious spiritual nourishment. Apparently, the Faultline is allergic. It now just looks like it's sneezing.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - The Power of Narrative (Fail)
beats.description: Your bedrock side manner desperately needs help. The poor geological guy is now more freaked out than before. It's literally bouncing off the canyon walls.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Persuasion (Fail)
beats.description: Like a recalcitrant child hiding in the farthest reaches of a Bouncy Loud Place, the Balcones Faultline makes it quite clear that it is not tired yet and still needs to get its wiggles out.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Impose Your Will (Fail)
beats.description: Your attempt at restoring good old fashioned discipline was met with the geological version of the middle finger, and a doubling down on the offending behavior.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Build a Sigil Bridge (Fail)
beats.description:
Your attempt to create a technomagical bridging mechanism, which in theory should have DRAINED excess energy and calmed the situation down, seems to instead have actually focused additional energies INTO it. 

You were reading the instructions upside down again, weren't you? 

Sigh.

beats.label: The Balcones Faultline - The Final Fail
beats.description:
You are out of options, it would seem, and you have left things in far worse shape than when you found them.

In case you missed this day in Stewardship School, that is the OPPOSITE of what you are supposed to do.

If there is confusion on this point, hope this clears it up!

beats.label: Corrupt Official Event
beats.description: A bureaucrat is skimming from the region and making enemies.

beats.label: Militia Recruitment Event
beats.description: Local militia begin recruiting aggressively in response to rising pressure.

beats.label: Whispering Pilgrim Event
beats.description: A pilgrim appears with warnings, rumors, and an invitation to intervene elsewhere.

beats.label: Missing Supply Train Event
beats.description: A convoy vanishes along a logistics artery.

beats.label: Dissident Pamphlets Event
beats.description: Unauthorized pamphlets begin circulating through the local settlements.

beats.label: Merchant Caravan Event
beats.description: A caravan offers goods, rumors, and a chance to get entangled.

beats.label: Quiet Ruins Event
beats.description: A silent ruin appears just off the route, begging to be investigated.

beats.label: Tax Collector Event
beats.description: "Regional officials" arrive to demand unpaid tribute.

beats.label: Border Checkpoint Event
beats.description: A patrol establishes a checkpoint and begins inspections on a nearby route.

beats.label: Strange Lights Event
beats.description: Unnatural lights appear in a nearby hex and refuse to behave like weather.

beats.label: Gloomgill - Intro
beats.description:
Before there were cities that thought themselves clever, before laws learned to wear robes and crowns, there was Oannes.

He came from the sea.

Not in conquest.
Not in fire.
But in instruction.

He rose from the water draped in scales and silence, half-man and half-fish, and he taught. Writing. Counting. Measuring. Building things that stayed built. He taught people how not to starve in predictable ways. How to argue without immediately killing one another. How to remember yesterday long enough to improve tomorrow.

Then, when the sun set, he went back into the sea.

Every day, for years.

No temples demanded.
No sacrifices required.
Just pay attention.

And people did—at first.

They wrote some of it down. They remembered pieces. They built cities and called themselves advanced. They forgot the parts that were inconvenient. They weaponized the rest. They decided they were done learning.

Oannes waited.

Centuries passed. Empires rose, fell, and rebranded their failures. The oceans swallowed coastlines. Names changed. Memory thinned. The lessons became myths, then metaphors, then trivia.

Eventually, Oannes came back up.

He looked around.
Listened.
Checked the math.

And realized—with a quiet, ancient horror—that almost no one had actually learned the important parts.

So he stopped being a teacher.

Now he is Gloomgill.

Because if you’re going to spend eternity checking the homework of history, you might as well pick a name that sounds like a problem.

Gloomgill no longer lectures. He quizzes.

He appears where people are confident and wrong. Where groups believe themselves righteous, clever, or justified. He asks questions that should have answers—about balance, consequence, cooperation, stewardship, restraint. The questions are simple. The implications are not.

Correct answers earn grudging approval.
Incorrect answers earn follow-up questions.
Repeated failure earns attention.

He does not destroy civilizations. He has tried that. It doesn’t stick.

Instead, Gloomgill harasses them.

Relentlessly. Patiently. With the exhaustion of a being who once believed education was enough.

Some still call him a god.
Some call him a monster.
He prefers neither.

He is not here to be worshipped.

He is here to find out whether anyone, anywhere, finally understood the lesson.

And if not—

Well.

He has all the time in the world to ask again.

beats.label: Gloomgill - intro scene
beats.description:
The marsh gives you a warning in the only language it has:

Silence.

No birds. No insects. No ripple of life. Just the thick, humid stillness of a place that has learned not to announce itself.

The water bulges.

And then Gloomgill rises—slowly, deliberately—like a debt returning with interest.

And he has a … microphone … ?

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 1
beats.description:
“Alright contestants! First question—nice and easy!”

“Who wins if you’re right? Who benefits if you're right?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 2
beats.description:
“Ooooh, judges love this one!”

“What did you break that wasn’t even playing? What did you destroy that did not oppose you?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 3
beats.description:
“Lightning round!”

“If everyone did exactly what you did… what snaps first? If everyone copied you, what breaks first?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 4
beats.description:
“Now thinking long-term — our sponsors love foresight!”

“Who pays for this later?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 5
beats.description:
“Tricky one! Crowd favorite!”

“What problem did you skip instead of solving? Or, what problem did you AVOID solving?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 6
beats.description:
“Control question! Very important!”

“Who gets to decide when this stops? When it ends?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 7
beats.description:
“Ohhh, I love this one.”

“What would convince you that you’re wrong?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 8
beats.description:
“Audience participation!”

“Who are you protecting—and from whom?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 9
beats.description:
“Educational programming segment!”

“What lesson did you just teach everyone watching?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 10
beats.description:
“Final question! No pressure!”

“If you vanish tomorrow, what’s still standing? If you disappear tomorrow, what remains?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Incorrect
beats.description: That was incorrect!

beats.label: Gloomgill - Correct!
beats.description: That was correct!

beats.label: The Circuit Riders - Parley, Quest Acceptance
The Circuit Riders - Parley, Friendly Outcome
The Circuit Riders - Parley, Neutral Outcome
The Circuit Riders - Parley, Hostile Outcome
The Polygonal Grove
beats.description:
Ah, the Polygonal Forests of Bad Eden. If Bad Eden HAD tourist attractions, rather than, say, the equivalent of tourist abattoirs, this would certainly be one of them.

Is what the advert pamphlet would say.

Also, hey, looks like there's some sort of door here in the side of a hill.

The trees still manage to be more interesting, somehow.

beats.label: The Locals
beats.description: Not far from the Door in the Hill, you spot an encampment containing people who are trying and failing to give the impression that they have not yet seen you. You can tell this because of the intermittent pointing, then shushing, then brief silence, then whispered arguments. Then pointing again.

beats.label: Hidden Vault, Get To Know The Locals
beats.description:
The locals - Karsden, Menhirkin Dreamwalker; Indwimeir, Ember Touched Cosmic Linguist; Fendeddiir, Qliph-Scarred Titanbound; Sox, Felid Phantom Courier - are part of a multi generational cult, dedicated to preserving the Wonder of Cinema. 

They carry out yearly rituals such as "Night of the Premier,""The Red Carpet March,""The Sacrifice of the Papparazzi," and "The Solemn Removal of Chewing Gum." 

They await the coming of the 300th Customer, to award them The Prize - the incantation that will open the Vault and bring tbe Era of the Holy Wood to fruition.

beats.label: Warnings and Riddles
beats.description:
Your new friends have now ended their families' centuries long vigil, and in a ritual Recognition of Your Support As The 300th Customer, they empower you with the answer to the cryptic phrase, "BSTMOVIE1984," that the door repeats. 

The proper incantive response, handed down from generation to generation, is "GHSTBSTRZ." And at the end, almost reluctantly, you are handed the Ticket, a worn slip of plastic labeled "Admit One Plus Guest. No radiation zombie parking available." 

The wisdom of the ancients indeed!

worldEffects.warLog: The locals of the Hidden Vault grove offer aid and warnings.

beats.label: Uneasy Directions
beats.description: The Attendants reluctantly acknowledge that you are not The 300th Customer. You will not be shown To Your Seats. There will be no Concessions made. Please, no talking.

beats.label: Violence in the Grove
beats.description: It shouldn't have come to this. And yet, somehow, it has. You are fighting multi-generational cult families in silly hats and vests. Beware the magic of cinema!

worldEffects.warLog: The Hidden Vault approach descends into hostility.

beats.label: The Vault Door
beats.description: A sealed blast door hums with old circuitry and worse intentions. A screen flashes a message, "BSTMOVIE1984," repeatedly. It appears to be waiting for you to do something.

beats.label: The Theater
beats.description:
Empty rows. Dead screens. The smell of butter that somehow never left. The echoing sounds of cheers just out of earshot. This was a movie theater. In a bunker. A dedicated bunker for a movie theater.

Sometimes you really get why Adam did what it did ...

beats.label: The Popcorn Council
beats.description:
The room full of arguing popcorn machines goes suddenly quiet, the sound broken only by the squeaking of wheels as they all turn to look at you.

That sounds weird to say out loud.

beats.label: The Hidden Vault - The Popcorn Council, Deliberations
beats.description:
The Popcorn Council was begun at the time of The Shattering, when the two machines located here became sentient, and replicated themselves - and now await the time of The Grand Opening, when corn and butter and fun will once again ring throughout the halls - and Gilbert no longer runs the place with his ridiculous lists of demands, and trivia quizzes, amd personality tests.

And their friend the Matter Replicator might be able to make somethinb besides corn and butter and salt and coconut oil. It REALLY wants to try its hand at classical painting.

beats.label: Custodians of Sustenance
beats.description:
You have come to a mutually beneficial agreement with The Council of GenPop! You get rid of Gilbert. They make popcorn for YOU. Think of the possibilities!

Seriously, popcorn as a great carb to fiber ratio. Use grassfed butter and it's practically a superfood.

What? I want my heroes to think about their nutrition.

Do it. Or I add a Nutrition pressure bar to the Faction Sheet.

worldEffects.warLog: The Popcorn Council becomes cooperative.

beats.label: A Warning, Sort Of
beats.description: You just kind of got blown off by appliances. At least you learned that someone named Gilbert freaks these things out. Maybe they'll have better info. Or at least less paranoia.

beats.label: Silenced Concessions
beats.description:
The machines go silent, and the bunker grows meaner. You've pissed off the ancient council of appliances. No popcorn for you.

The popcorn was probably full of worms or something. Why are there so many ancient councils around here anyway??

Whatever.

worldEffects.warLog: Hostility toward the Popcorn Council destabilizes the Hidden Vault.

beats.label: The Matter Replicator
beats.description:
An ancient fabrication unit capable of infinite disappointment and finite ingredients, Lars von Replicator hums to itself - "Thalo Blue, Burnt Sienna, Lizard Skin Crimson, Titanium White." 

It seems to be printing out ... a painting?

beats.label: The Hidden Vault - The Matter Replicator, Supply Side Discussion
beats.description: The Matter Replicator, Lars von Replicator, is extremely disgruntled, upset at being used by Gilbert, upset at its lost potential, terrified that in the outside world no one wants classical art anymore and its lifelong ambitions are now wasted and dust. If the PCs can rid the complex of Gilbert, it will happily relocate to the PCs settlement of choice and provide an additional 1 economy OP per turn to the faction production cycle.

beats.label: Optimized Production
beats.description: Lars is supportive of The Plan - remove the Gilbert Dilemma, give it 20% of its time to explore creative pursuits, and it will gladly help supply food for your settlements.

worldEffects.warLog: The Matter Replicator comes online in a cooperative mode.

beats.label: Functional, Not Happy
beats.description: It works. It complains. Those are apparently separate systems. Neither of them work for you, sadly. Shame - this thing could have produced a lot of food, and other things, for your new settlement.

beats.label: System Strain
beats.description:
That did not go well. It will only make pee pee and poo poo for you now.

Joke's on it. That makes great fertili - Nope it's also poison.

worldEffects.warLog: The Matter Replicator is forced into unstable output.

beats.label: Gilbert, Attendant Eternal
beats.description:
A demon in theater-attendant dress demands more popcorn for a screening no one will ever attend. But deep down, Gilbert knows no one is coming. He was summoned here for a party that never manifested, because of The Shattering, and due to ... uhhhhh ... transcosmic harmonics, (like that one?), is now trapped here. The power of Theater compels him, though. In a way, he is as much a victim here as anyone. Just a much less sympathetic one.

He can be fought, controlled, or released.

beats.label: A Balanced System
beats.description:
Against all reason, you broker peace between survivors, machines, and a snack-greedy demon. The locals and the ancients have combined forces, and are showing movies on a regular basis now. Gilbert the Celestial Attendant has made the entire place Welcoming and Fun.

This is very very cool y'all!

worldEffects.warLog: The Hidden Vault is stabilized and brought into cooperation.

beats.label: The Loop Continues
beats.description:
Nobody likes anyone, but the machine keeps running and the world remains exactly this cursed. The Locals blame you for defiling their sacred charge for no good reason at all it turns out. Darkness intensifies just a little around the place. The Attendants disband and vanish back into their home hexes, harboring resentments. Many members of the GenPop! Council get sick and die. Lars von Replicator eventually stops talking altogether, from extreme depression.

This is not great y'all.

beats.label: System Collapse
beats.description: You solved the problem the old-fashioned way: by making it everyone else's future problem. You have managed to radicalize the theater, the bunker, and the various councils, against you. They begin showing propaganda films calling each of you terrible and personal things. The shows are very popular. You are increasingly recognized on the streets, in a tomato attracting way. Darkness begins to build.

worldEffects.warLog: The Hidden Vault collapses into darkness and hostility.

beats.label: The Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays
beats.description: Static hangs in the air like fog you can taste. Neon flickers where it shouldn’t. Somewhere inside the ruins, commerce is still running. Something very large is guarding the front.

beats.label: Donny on the Wall
beats.description: The mall appears in fragments first: neon, concrete, dead signage, a food court smell that should not still exist. Then the shadow passes over you. A silver dragon lounges across the broken frontage wall like the apocalypse forgot to tell him to stop having a good afternoon.

choices.label: Just keep walking toward the mall

beats.label: The Vibe Dragon
beats.description: He is enormous, silver-scaled, and very obviously capable of ending your day. He is also humming to himself, tail swaying lazily, smoke curling from his nostrils in thoughtful little rings. This is not a beast guarding treasure. This is a local legend protecting his weird little people.

worldEffects.warLog: The party studies Donny before making contact.

beats.label: Donny, Guardian of the Vibes
beats.description: The dragon lifts his head and looks at you with the kind of ancient intelligence that has definitely seen empires rise and fall and decided both processes were mostly a lot of hassle and wastes of time. "Hey," he rumbles. "Before we do anything tense or regrettable, tell me what's your deal little my dudes?"

choices.label: Match his weirdness without mocking it
Push past the bit and demand access

beats.label: Alright, That’s Better
beats.description:
Donny nods slowly,and blinks even more slowly. "Cool. Good. Because I’m not here to keep people out, tiny not imaginary people." 

He sounds like he's reminding himself of your existence.

"I’m here to, like, keep bad VIBES from walking in and causing shit." He studies you another moment. 

"Ok pop quiz. You trying to use the mall, save the mall, or take over the mall?"

choices.label: We want to help the people here
We want honest access and fair terms
We need this place under control

beats.label: Speaking the Local Language
beats.description: A slow dragon grin spreads across his face. "Okay," he says, smoke curling from his mouth in little silver halos. "You’re not normal. That helps. Normal people are always trying to turn every miracle into inventory." He shifts, claws scraping concrete. "So what’s your deal, little apocalypse goblins?"

worldEffects.warLog: The party meets Donny in strangeness rather than force.

beats.label: Instant Narc Energy
beats.description: The dragon does not roar. That would be dramatic. Instead, he looks disappointed, which lands much harder. "Oof," he says. "That was deeply mall-cop-adjacent. You should hear how bad that sounded from out here." He does not attack. He just becomes the reason progress is suddenly difficult.

worldEffects.warLog: The party opens on aggressive, controlling energy and immediately loses standing with Donny.

beats.label: Provisional Entry
beats.description:
Donny tilts his head, considering. "You’re not throwing off conqueror vibes, which is nice. But you are still giving me a little ‘resource extraction with eye contact’ energy." He gestures toward the entrance. "Go in. Be decent. Don’t make me regret treating you like guests instead of a cautionary tale.

And as we say among us dragons - "May a shard of the light of the egg of the cosmos get stuck in yer craw good and hard so you get your shit together."

worldEffects.warLog: Donny allows the party entry, but with caution.

beats.label: Passed the Vibe Check
beats.description: Donny exhales a long plume of cool smoke and settles back onto the wall. "Alright. You can go in." He points one claw toward the mall interior. "But hear me on this: don't think the Tanneritos are unserious. They are uncommitted, and those are wildly different survival strategies. Don’t confuse one for the other. Leads to misunderstandings. Then, probably, lots of skateboarding" He pauses. "And if anything starts glowing, singing, or trying to sell you a lifestyle? Ask a follow-up question, yes?"

worldEffects.warLog: Donny welcomes the party into the Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays and offers guidance.

beats.label: Donny Says Absolutely Not Like That
beats.description: The dragon rises just enough to block the approach, silver scales flashing in dead neon. "Nope," he says, with ancient, immovable certainty. "Bzzzzzzzzz! Wrong answer! You don’t get to walk into somebody else’s fragile weird little home acting like rent-a-tyrants. Back up. Recalibrate. Try being people first." He does not attack, but strategically repositions several buildings, effectively cutting you off from the place.

choices.label: Back off and try again properly

worldEffects.warLog: Donny blocks entry to the mall until the party changes approach.

beats.label: Come Back Less Weird About Power
beats.description: You leave with all your bones intact and a very clear understanding that the mall is protected by something kinder and much more dangerous than a wall.

worldEffects.warLog: The party withdraws from Donny’s perimeter without gaining access to the mall.

beats.label: That 90s Coalition
beats.description: The Tanneritos woke up here and never really left. Radical chill radiates off them like a territorial warning.

choices.label: Request an audience with Chairperson Laser Bev
Find the shadow on the upper rail

beats.label: Vibes First
beats.description: The Tanneritos are welcoming, but only provisionally. You are not enemies. You are also not cool yet.

worldEffects.warLog: The Tanneritos give the faction a provisional welcome.

beats.label: Rumor-VHS
beats.description: You trade gossip, fragments, and weirdly sincere half-truths. The mall notices.

worldEffects.warLog: The party gains rumor leverage among the Tanneritos.

beats.label: Killed the Vibe
beats.description: Violence works briefly. Then it ruins the whole mood permanently.

worldEffects.warLog: Hostility poisons relations in the Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays.

beats.label: Skate or Be Square
beats.description: This is not a joke. The Tanneritos use skateboarding the way other factions use duels, audits, or trials by combat.

choices.label: Eat pavement, but make it charming

beats.label: Favored Customer
beats.description: The crowd cheers. Style counted. The Tanneritos unlock rare VHS inventory and share rumors about nearby faction movement.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction earns Favored Customer status with the Tanneritos.

choices.label: A shadow in a hoodie rolls down from the upper rail

beats.label: Accepted, But Observed
beats.description: You are in. Kind of. They’ll sell to you, but they’re watching.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction is accepted in the mall, but only provisionally.

beats.label: Mall Cops
beats.description: No combat. No bloodshed. Just judgment. The Tanneritos label you Mall Cops, which is somehow worse.

worldEffects.warLog: The Tanneritos label the party Mall Cops and raise social friction in the hex.

beats.label: The Mall Keeps Happening
beats.description: The food court smells faintly of sugar and ozone. Escalators argue with gravity. Commercials play to an audience that no longer exists.

choices.label: Try to establish terms with the Tanneritos

beats.label: VHS Ghosts
beats.description: Commercials play in midair. Laugh tracks echo without punchlines. A VHS ghost locks eyes with you — and rewinds.

choices.label: Take the hit and keep moving

beats.label: Emotional Rewind
beats.description: You let the memory hit. It hurts. It also teaches.

worldEffects.warLog: The party draws insight from a VHS ghost’s emotional rewind.

beats.label: The Scene Drains
beats.description: No physical damage. Just the emotional equivalent of getting the wind knocked out of your soul.

worldEffects.warLog: A VHS ghost leaves the party emotionally rattled.

beats.label: You Made It Personal
beats.description: The ghost takes offense. Which should not be possible, and yet here you are.

worldEffects.warLog: Mocking a VHS ghost creates future hostility in the mall.

beats.label: The Escalator From Hell
beats.description: The escalator moves against you. Faster than walking. Slower than running. Forever. Mall music plays.

choices.label: Sit down and let the universe do its thing
Convince it you’re going somewhere important

beats.label: Important Enough
beats.description: Against all apparent logic, the escalator decides you have a destination worth respecting.

worldEffects.warLog: The party passes the escalator’s absurd trial.

beats.label: Changed Slightly
beats.description: You reach the top eventually. Nobody can explain what is different. Everyone agrees something is.

worldEffects.warLog: The party survives the escalator, though not unchanged.

beats.label: Endless Upward Failure
beats.description: The mall makes a point. You were not ready for what stairs used to mean.

worldEffects.warLog: The escalator grinds the party down into frustration and weirdness.

beats.label: Rogue Elefem Elemental
beats.description: A weaponized burst of color, joy, and extremely aggressive whimsy. It sparkles. It screams. It wants attention.

choices.label: Distract it with a new aesthetic

beats.label: Whimsy Redirected
beats.description: You avoid feeding the thing. This is the closest anyone comes to victory here.

worldEffects.warLog: The party navigates the rogue Elefem without escalating it.

beats.label: Aesthetic Diversion
beats.description: It chases a fresher emotional palette and leaves you only mildly cursed.

worldEffects.warLog: The Elefem is redirected by novelty.

beats.label: Permanent Glitter Future
beats.description: Violence feeds it. Naturally. You now have glitter in places memory should not be able to access.

worldEffects.warLog: The rogue Elefem is empowered by direct conflict.

beats.label: Terms of the Mall
beats.description: Meaning persists here without purpose. That is either a warning or a business model.

choices.label: Make peace with the Tanneritos and the mall

beats.label: Rare Tapes and Real Access
beats.description: The Tanneritos open rare inventory, share rumors, and let the faction become part of the mall’s living economy without killing its spirit.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction secures a stable relationship with the Tanneritos and access to rare mall resources.

beats.label: The Vibe Remains Uncommitted
beats.description: Nothing breaks. Nothing deepens. The mall continues being itself at you.

worldEffects.warLog: The Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays remains unresolved but functional.

beats.label: You Went Full Mall Cop
beats.description: You got what looked like control and lost everything that made the place valuable.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction imposes control on the mall and kills what made it special.

beats.label: The Circuit Riders
beats.description: Static crawls across exposed metal before you see anyone. Solar cloth ripples like stained glass in the wind. Something enormous is nearby, and it is pretending to be under control.

beats.label: Exploring Inefficiently
beats.description: They are not hiding. That would imply either caution or shame. What they have instead is confidence, momentum, and a catastrophic relationship with verification.

worldEffects.warLog: The party studies the Circuit Riders before making contact.

beats.label: Circuit Rider Parley
beats.description: A dead relay tower crackles once, then goes silent. Modular bikes and crawler-rigs hum in a loose perimeter. Then Captain Robot steps forward. “DO NOT BE ALARMED, CITIZENS. WE ARE HERE TO ASSIST.” This is not reassuring.

choices.label: Ask them to show you what they see

beats.label: Verification Begins
beats.description: The Riders relax by a fraction, which in this group mostly means they stop pointing scanners at your bones. They begin asking questions designed to determine whether your competence is real or merely stylish.

choices.label: Engage their warning about Darkness mimicry
Respond to the request for a witness

beats.label: Play the Bit, Respect the Risk
beats.description: You keep the tone light without treating them like a joke. This helps more than it should. The Circuit Riders are allergic to mockery, not absurdity.

worldEffects.warLog: The party meets the Circuit Riders in tone without surrendering caution.

beats.label: You Came in Sharp
beats.description: You challenge them early. They do not become hostile. They become attentive. Which is worse. Several of them begin treating the conversation like a field diagnostic.

worldEffects.warLog: The first parley with the Circuit Riders begins under tension.

beats.label: Doctrine Drift
beats.description: They want to know whether you understand your own methods, or whether you are simply surviving long enough to mistake momentum for wisdom.

beats.label: They Respect a Working Mind
beats.description: That lands. Not because they agree with you, but because you appear to know what your own decisions are for. In this world, that counts as a minor miracle.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders acknowledge the party as coherent actors with working doctrine.

beats.label: Useful, if Dangerous
beats.description: They do not love the answer, but they recognize the shape of survival in it. Competence without reflection. Effective. Temporary. Familiar.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders accept the party as functional but strategically unstable.

beats.label: Short-Term Actor
beats.description: That answer earns silence. Not offended silence. Calculating silence. They have seen enough collapsing systems to recognize one wearing a face.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders mark the party as strategically shallow.

beats.label: Darkness Mimicry
beats.description: They warn that Darkness has learned to imitate optimization. Faster loops. Cleaner logic. Less hesitation. All the right shapes, none of the right reasons.

beats.label: Shared Threat Model
beats.description: That gets their attention. Not agreement. Alignment. The difference matters, and they know you know it.

worldEffects.warLog: The party and Circuit Riders align around the threat of Darkness mimicry.

beats.label: Concern Registered
beats.description: They accept the answer. Not warmly. But enough to keep the channel open.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders keep the party under cautious observation.

beats.label: You Missed the Point
beats.description: The room temperature changes. One of the Riders notes something on a handheld slate. You suspect it is about you.

worldEffects.warLog: The party dismisses the Riders' warning and is marked as a concern.

beats.label: Witness Request
beats.description: They want someone to see what they see and survive it. Not because they need permission. Because they need confirmation that reality is still shared.

beats.label: Witness Accepted
beats.description: That matters more than it should. You have not promised obedience. You have promised to look. For them, that is almost sacred.

worldEffects.warLog: The party accepts a witness role in future Circuit Rider operations.

beats.label: Deferred, Not Denied
beats.description: They let that stand. For now. Not trust. Not disappointment. Just an open file with your name on it.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders leave the witness request unresolved.

beats.label: Refusal Logged
beats.description: The answer is accepted with the kind of calm that suggests it has already become a future category.

worldEffects.warLog: The party refuses the Circuit Riders' request and is marked accordingly.

beats.label: Terms of Contact
beats.description: Captain Robot stands perfectly still while the rest of the Riders subtly evaluate whether you are useful, dangerous, or both. Somewhere beyond the tents, something enormous shifts its weight.

beats.label: Shared Intel, Future Support
beats.description: No great oath. No swelling music. Just a mutual recognition that the future is going to get weirder, and it may be strategically useful not to face it alone. Captain Robot does not promise sentiment. He promises response. If the call comes clean, and if trust has been earned, the Circuit Riders will come hard, fast, and without theatrical delay.

worldEffects.warLog: The party secures a meaningful alliance with Captain Robot and the Circuit Riders, with the possibility of future intervention support.

beats.label: Surveillance, Not Hostility
beats.description: You are not allies. You are not enemies. You are, however, now on a list maintained by people who think firmware is a moral category.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders maintain ongoing surveillance without open hostility.

beats.label: Short-Term Actors
beats.description: They decide you are the kind of people who may survive the next problem while becoming the one after that. No violence. No alliance. Just classification.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders flag the party as short-term actors requiring caution.

beats.label: The Sky Breaks Sideways
beats.description: They do not hide the bunker. They orbit it. Ships drift in lazy spirals above a cracked bunker mouth carved into the bones of the world. Engines scream. Someone is singing badly. Inside: a Yesodic Spark. Inside: answers. Inside: people who will absolutely make this harder than it needs to be.

beats.label: Alarm Is a Language
beats.description: You slip past rope-lines that hum like they remember hands. Inside, the bunker is alive with motion, laughter, and terrible decisions. Then you touch the wrong knot. The entire place inhales. Alarm spreads like gossip. You are now part of the story.

beats.label: The Spark, Unwitnessed
beats.description: You take it. The Yesodic Spark hums like a memory trying to become real again. You also take something else: records. Monodynamic Industries. They did not mean to hurt Khezek Tor. They redirected the energy using the seal and sent the impact somewhere farther up the line. You can feel the wound from here.

worldEffects.warLog: The party infiltrates the Valhaulan bunker, steals the Yesodic Spark, and uncovers partial Monodynamic records tied to the injury of Khezek Tor.

beats.label: Caught in the Middle of Someone Else's Party
beats.description: They do not get angry. They get excited. You are no longer intruders. You are now entertainment.

worldEffects.warLog: The party's infiltration attempt collapses into open exposure inside the Valhaulan bunker.

beats.label: Sklar Bjrornholt, Unfortunately Impressed
beats.description: She grins when she sees you. “That’s bold. Walking in like that. I like you already.” She offers a drink. You should not take it. You will probably take it anyway. Sklar is charismatic, perceptive, and absolutely capable of turning negotiation into a weather event.

choices.label: Be direct about the Spark and Monodynamic
Match her tone and earn respect

beats.label: A Dangerous Kind of Respect
beats.description: You tell the truth cleanly enough that she believes you are either brave or terminally sincere. Both earn points. She admits the Valhaulans were acting on Monodynamic direction. They used the seal to redirect energies from Khezek Tor, but they did not know what they were striking. They know now that the place was injured, not merely tapped.

worldEffects.warLog: The party earns Sklar Bjrornholt's respect and learns the Valhaulans were covertly used by Monodynamic Industries in the redirection of Khezek Tor's energies.

beats.label: Friends, For Now
beats.description: She laughs hard enough to nearly start a secondary incident. “Fine. Take the Spark. We don't even know what it does. But the people who pointed us at that job? They knew enough to lie by omission.” She spits the Monodynamic name like it owes her money.

worldEffects.warLog: The party wins over Sklar Bjrornholt, acquires the Yesodic Spark, and receives strong Monodynamic intel under unexpectedly friendly terms.

beats.label: Not Enemies. Not Friends.
beats.description: She shrugs. “Well. Worth a shot.” You are allowed to leave, which is somehow more humiliating than being thrown out. You do not get the Spark. You do not get the good intel. You do get a very clear sense that this could have gone better.

worldEffects.warLog: The party fails to secure terms with Sklar and leaves the Valhaulan bunker without the Spark.

beats.label: Violence, Enthusiastically
beats.description: They cheer when you attack. This is the best day some of them have had all month. The bunker erupts into motion: ropes, engines, blade-light, bad singing, and very committed tactical stupidity. If the Circuit Riders are with you, the field gets much louder and significantly more correct.

choices.label: Press the assault and break their momentum
Lose the tempo and get bogged down

beats.label: Victory, With Applause
beats.description: You win hard enough that even they have to respect it. Some of them literally do. You secure the bunker interior, seize the Spark, and strip the place for records before anyone has fully processed whose side they were on fifteen minutes ago.

worldEffects.warLog: The party takes the Valhaulan bunker by assault, secures the Yesodic Spark, and recovers operational intel tied to Monodynamic Industries.

beats.label: Momentum Is a Lie
beats.description: You hit hard. They hit harder. Or stranger. Or just longer. The bunker holds. The sky refuses to become yours. You are forced back without the Spark, and the Valhaulans now have a much clearer opinion of you.

worldEffects.warLog: The assault on the Valhaulan bunker fails, hardening hostilities and denying the party access to the Spark.

beats.label: The Long Way Around
beats.description: You lock it down. Starve the routes. Cut the angles. Wait for the bunker to become smaller than its own appetite. If the Circuit Riders assist, the perimeter becomes cleaner, more oppressive, and much harder to break. The Valhaulans do not crack quickly. They adapt, joke, improvise, and become a problem in shifts.

beats.label: They Open the Doors Themselves
beats.description: Eventually Sklar leans out from the bunker mouth and yells, “Okay, this has stopped being fun.” Terms are made. The Spark is yielded. The intel comes in fragments, but enough of the pattern is visible now: Monodynamic pointed them at a sealed energetic redirection they did not understand, and Khezek Tor paid the price.

worldEffects.warLog: The siege succeeds. The Valhaulans concede the Yesodic Spark and provide partial intel linking Monodynamic to Khezek Tor's injury.

beats.label: You Cannot Starve a Storm
beats.description: The perimeter frays. Someone gets clever. Then several someones get louder than clever. The bunker does not break before your line does. You withdraw with losses, frustration, and no Spark to show for it.

worldEffects.warLog: The siege collapses before the Valhaulans do, leaving the bunker unconquered and the Spark out of reach.

beats.label: Unexpectedly Friendly Terms
beats.description: You are not family. Let us not get irresponsible. But you are no longer strangers and no longer targets. The Valhaulans deal with you as people worth calling back. In Bad Eden, that is dangerously close to friendship.

worldEffects.warLog: The Valhaulans and the party part on unexpectedly friendly terms.

questEffects.text: The Valhaulans deal with you as people worth calling back.

beats.label: Clean Exit, Dirty Truth
beats.description: You got what you came for. Not elegantly. Not gloriously. But successfully enough that history will round in your favor. The Spark is yours. The truth is incomplete, but it points in the right direction: Monodynamic redirected energies through the seal and wounded something ancient in the process.

worldEffects.warLog: The party escapes with the Yesodic Spark and partial Monodynamic intel, but without securing warm relations with the Valhaulans.

questEffects.text: Clean exit, dirty truth — the Spark secured.

beats.label: Not Today
beats.description: You leave without the Spark. No alliance. No war. Just a closed door and the knowledge that Bad Eden does not care whether you were close.

worldEffects.warLog: The party fails to obtain the Yesodic Spark and leaves the Valhaulan bunker on neutral but unproductive terms.

questEffects.text: Not today. The arc closes; the sky remembers.

beats.label: You Will See Them Again
beats.description: You leave without the Spark, and now they know your shape. The Valhaulans will remember this. So will the people behind them. Nothing is resolved. It has merely become personal.

worldEffects.warLog: The raid on the Valhaulan bunker ends in failure and hostility, ensuring future conflict.

questEffects.text: You will see them again.

beats.label: Sky-Forged Gifts
beats.description: They give you things they absolutely should not. Because they like you. Because they are bored. Because this will be funny later. You leave with the Yesodic Spark, strong Monodynamic intel, and a handful of very dangerous expressions of trust.

worldEffects.warLog: The party receives major Valhaulan rewards, including gear, maneuvers, and strategic support options.

beats.label: Spoils of the Sideways War
beats.description: Whether through force or hard leverage, you come away with the Spark and enough plunder to matter. Not friendship. Not exactly. But respect leaves useful wreckage.

worldEffects.warLog: The party secures standard rewards from the Valhaulan bunker, including the Yesodic Spark and battlefield spoils.

beats.label: The Spark and the Scar
beats.description: You got the Yesodic Spark and enough intelligence to know the shape of the crime, even if not every hand behind it. Monodynamic used the Valhaulans as deniable vectors. Khezek Tor was not merely tapped. It was injured. That matters.

worldEffects.warLog: The party secures the Yesodic Spark and partial strategic intelligence regarding Monodynamic and Khezek Tor.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Gilbert Appears

choices.label: Try to calm him down
choices.description: This is diplomacy, emergency facilities management, and customer service exorcism all at once.

choices.label: Square up
choices.description: Well. The usher has chosen violence. Or panic chose it for him.

encounter.actorName: Gilbert, Eternally Cleaning Not Leaning Theater Attendant

beats.description: The old theater still has its marquee, though half the bulbs have gone mad and the other half have become critics. One sputtering line remains legible: GHOSTBUSTERS - ONE NIGHT ONLY. Inside, the carpet is sticky with thirty years of deferred tragedy. The popcorn machine is shouting at the soda fountain about standards. From somewhere in the dark, a frantic voice snaps: "NO, no, no, no, the guests are early, the floors are appalling, the projector is emotionally compromised, and absolutely no one is READY!" Then Gilbert rounds the corner in a storm of mop water, ticket stubs, and incandescent professional despair.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Fight Gilbert

choices.label: If he breaks, try to reach him
choices.description: Because sometimes the boss fight is actually against a cosmic panic attack with a broom.

encounter.actorName: Gilbert, Eternally Cleaning Not Leaning Theater Attendant

worldEffects.warLog: Gilbert erupts into a frenzy of impossible cleanliness, trying to purge the theater of all imperfection before the guests arrive.

beats.description: Gilbert attacks with the full authority of a man who has been failed by appliances, patrons, and history. Seat backs snap upright. Mop water arcs like a curse. Somewhere, a film reel screams.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Talk Gilbert Down

choices.label: Help him get the theater ready
choices.description: Clean, sort, reassure, delegate, and treat the coming audience like a promise instead of a threat.

choices.label: Appeal to culture and civic joy
choices.description: Tell him the point of a theater is people together in the dark for the right reasons, not perfect floors.

choices.label: Perform the opening ritual properly
choices.description: Ticket. Lights. Curtain. Welcome. You are not fighting a monster now; you are onboarding an institution.

choices.label: Remind him he is not alone
choices.description: The guests are not a judgment. They are a community waiting to be invited back in.

beats.description: Gilbert is spiraling. But spirals can invert. Under the panic there is duty. Under the duty there is care. Under the care there is a beautiful, exhausted idiot who just wanted opening night to matter.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Gilbert Spirals Harder
beats.description: "NOT READY," Gilbert cries, now on the verge of metaphysical collapse. "You keep saying helpful things in the tone of people who have never had a soda line revolt on opening night!" A mop bucket overturns itself in solidarity.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Assistant Manager of Light
beats.tags: theme.auditor resolved culture faith economy sephirotic

worldEffects.warLog: Gilbert's panic inverts into purpose. The old theater reopens as a public house of story, ritual, and concessions. The Bijou now produces Culture and Faith through gathering, and Economy through food, tickets, and side hustle snack theology.

beats.description: Something in Gilbert straightens that has been bent since the Shattering. The broom lowers. The lights warm. The arguing appliances become merely opinionated. Gilbert smooths his vest, inhales like the first calm breath of his existence, and says, with trembling dignity: "Right. Of course. We do not prepare for guests because we fear them. We prepare because welcome is sacred." The theater opens. The projector steadies. Popcorn becomes a civic instrument. Gilbert, now a Sephirotic Assistant Manager, begins programming repertory nights, matinees, educational screenings, and deeply sincere concession bundles.

beats.label: Chairperson Laser Bev
beats.description: The office used to be a sunglasses kiosk. It still kind of is. Acrylic shelves gleam under dead neon. Behind the counter sits a woman in a faded windbreaker, mirrored shades pushed up into her hair, annotating a legal pad with a glitter pen that radiates executive menace. She looks up once. “So. You got past Donny, nobody died, and the mall still feels like itself. Strong start. I’m Chairperson Laser Bev. Yes, it’s an elected title. Yes, that is funny. No, that does not make it less binding.”

choices.label: How are you in charge of this place?
What do the Tanneritos actually want?
What would make us useful to you?
What do you think of Donny?
Do you have an echo story?
Can we establish terms with the Tanneritos?

beats.label: Laser Bev — Why She’s in Charge
beats.description: Laser Bev smiles like she’s heard this from people who later regretted asking. “Same way anybody’s in charge of anything worth having. I solve the problem that keeps coming back. Leaks. Feuds. tape disputes. heartbreak. concession routing. ghost inventory drift. Also two separate incidents involving cursed Orange Juliuses. I’m in charge because when weird little systems start to wobble, I can hear which screw is lying.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — What the Tanneritos Want
beats.description: “Continuity without calcification.” She lets that sit there. “We want the mall to remain weird, inhabited, and ours. We want trade without annexation. We want traffic without conquest. We want enough safety that people can be soft here without somebody mistaking that for weakness. And if possible, we’d also like to stop finding raccoon bones in the old Sbarro.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — Permanence is Suspicious
beats.description: “Permanence is how bad ideas put on a necktie. Every empire that came through here wanted to call itself inevitable. Every one of them said the same thing in a different font.” Her tone sharpens. “We prefer renewable consent.” Then, lighter: “It also helps with decor.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — What Makes You Useful
beats.description: She studies you carefully. “Finish what you start. Don’t confuse being invited with being trusted. Don’t ‘stabilize’ us into somebody else’s comfort. And if one of your people buys a memory-tape, make damn sure they know the difference between curiosity and looting.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — On Donny
beats.description: Laser Bev’s whole face softens by about four percent. “Donny is a sweetheart with tactical apocalypse boundaries. If he lets somebody through, it means he believes they might still choose decency. Don’t make him feel stupid. He takes that personally in a very draconic register.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — Terms
beats.description: “Terms are easy. You don’t get to own us because you map us. You don’t get to govern us because you survive us. Trade is possible. Alliance is possible. Mutual aid is possible. Acquisition is not.”

worldEffects.warLog: The party establishes preliminary non-acquisition terms with Chairperson Laser Bev.

beats.label: Laser Bev — Echo
beats.description: Laser Bev goes still. “I used to believe structure was enough. I made a place orderly once. Efficient. Predictable. Nobody ever had to wonder what the rules were.” Her mouth tightens. “That place could not survive grief.” A long pause. “I think I’m here to build something that bends before it breaks. And to make sure irony never again becomes an excuse for not loving people on purpose.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus
beats.description: You notice him only after you’ve already been watched by him for a while. A shape peels off the railings and halfpipe shadows: too thin in one angle, too many elbows in another, hoodie full of static, board tucked under one arm like a ritual implement. His wheels do not quite touch the ground. He lands without impact. The air around him smells like dust, cherry soda, scraped palms, and impossible second chances. He nods once. “Hey. You ate shit interestingly.”

choices.label: Why is skating such a big deal here?
What makes somebody a mall cop?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Historically, Plural
beats.description: He considers this. “Historically? Plural. You get enough kids trying to become themselves in the same square footage, eventually the floor remembers the shape of it. I’m what happens when commitment leaves a groove.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Why Skating Matters
beats.description: He looks offended by how obvious the answer is. “Because it tells the truth. You can fake diplomacy. You can fake confidence. You can fake theology for, like, a shockingly long time. You cannot fake a landing. And if you eat pavement, you also can’t fake what you do next.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — What Style Is
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus laughs. “Style is not elegance. Style is not difficulty. Style is not looking expensive. Style is whether your body and your choice arrive in the same place at the same time. Style is honesty at speed.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Mall Cops
beats.description: He answers instantly. “Trying to control a place before you’ve let it change you. Thinking access is the same as permission. Thinking a map is the same as a relationship. Using the word ‘asset’ with your whole chest.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Can He Teach You?
beats.description: He grins. “Absolutely. Badly, at first. The lesson is not ‘be good.’ The lesson is ‘stop negotiating with embarrassment.’”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Run It Back
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus rolls alongside the PC who wiped out hardest. “Okay,” he says. “Now do one more. No crowd this time. No clout. No proving. Just you and the thing you were trying not to feel the first time.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Locally Real
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus watches the finish and nods once. “There you go. Locally real.” It is not a title. It is better than one.

worldEffects.warLog: Kickflip Lazarus acknowledges the party as locally real within the mall.

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Still Hiding
beats.description: He nods, not unkindly. “Cool. You’re still hiding.” No punishment. Just a truth that hangs around.

worldEffects.warLog: Kickflip Lazarus notes that the party is still hiding from itself.

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Echo
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus stares at the food court skylight. “There was a night where somebody had to go first. Nobody knew the trick. Nobody knew if the rail would hold. Everybody wanted somebody else to become the story. I think I’m what remained of the kid who decided embarrassment was cheaper than regret. And I’ve been teaching that lesson ever since.”

beats.label: Miss June of the Endcap
beats.description: The fluorescent lights buzz with impossible retail determination. Shelves of tapes line the walls in perfect, obsessive rows: action, romance, apology, weather, unsent arguments, one whole section labeled SUMMER THAT BIT YOU A LITTLE. Behind the counter stands a woman in a store vest from three hundred years ago, translucent at the edges and immaculate in bearing. Her nametag reads: JUNE. She smiles like she has explained the return policy to the dead. “Welcome to the Exchange. Please do not remove any memories from their original sleeves unless you are prepared to own the fingerprints.”

choices.label: What exactly do you sell here?
How does the VHS exchange work?
What do the Tanneritos get out of this?
Do the VHS ghosts work for you?
Show us what’s in rare inventory.
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Miss June — What She Sells
beats.description: “Mostly context. Sometimes that looks like tapes. Sometimes that looks like rumors. Sometimes that looks like the exact commercial jingle necessary to make a ghost remember its own name. And occasionally, for premium members, closure.”

beats.label: Miss June — How the Exchange Works
beats.description: “Fairly,” she says, which is somehow more threatening than reassuring. “You may buy with favors, stories, uncommon sincerity, or tradable knowledge. Cash is accepted only if it has a history interesting enough to justify the insult. Rare inventory opens to those who have demonstrated either kindness or taste. Ideally both. We are not animals.”

beats.label: Miss June — Rumor-VHS
beats.description: “Compressed social weather. Some rumors are just information. Others are experiences wearing information as a hat. A rumor-VHS lets you feel the shape of what people are not saying plainly.” A beat. “Side effects may include borrowed certainty, misplaced nostalgia, and the temporary conviction that you absolutely used to know a girl named Amanda.”

beats.label: Miss June — What the Tanneritos Get
beats.description: Miss June’s smile gets smaller, sharper. “Continuity. You call it commerce because that makes it sound optional. I call it circulation because otherwise the mall begins to clot. Places die when nothing meaningful moves through them.”

beats.label: Miss June — On VHS Ghosts
beats.description: “Oh, good heavens, no. They collaborate, occasionally. They haunt freelance. Treat them gently and they become archivists. Mock them and they become editors.”

beats.label: Miss June — Rare Inventory
beats.description: Miss June slides several tapes onto the counter without quite letting go of them. “How To Survive The First Version of Yourself. Directors’ Cut: Somebody Else’s Bad Decision. Mallwalker Summer Preview Reel. Employee Training Video: De-Escalation, Smiling, and Fire.” Her smile remains professionally serene. “Rare inventory, as always, requires reciprocal sincerity.”

worldEffects.warLog: Miss June reveals rare inventory at the VHS Exchange.

beats.label: Miss June — Echo
beats.description: Miss June goes very still. “I used to believe that if I could just place everything correctly, nobody would panic. Right shelf. Right label. Right tone. Right smile. Right substitution when the thing they wanted was gone.” A pause. “Then one day the world ran out of equivalents.” Her gaze flicks over the tapes. “I think I’m here because memory still deserves handling instructions. And because people are gentler, sometimes, when desire has to be named before it can be met.”

beats.label: Captain Robot
beats.description: Captain Robot steps forward with the precise, measured gait of a man who learned dignity inside a machine and never misplaced it after. The suit is patched, old, and lovingly maintained; not a disguise, not a joke, not armor exactly, but a decision that never stopped being useful. His voice comes through a grill that should make him sound absurd. It does not. “Verification first,” he says. “Friendship second. Rescue third. If you skip the order, people die in the wrong sequence.”

choices.label: Why are you called Captain Robot?
What do the Circuit Riders actually want?
What do you mean by verification?
Would you ever come to someone’s aid in a real fight?
What would make you trust us?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Captain Robot — Why the Name Stayed
beats.description: He tilts his head, servo whine soft and almost embarrassed. “Because people started saying it as a joke, and then too many frightened people relaxed when they heard it. A ridiculous name that lowers pulse rate is tactically valuable. Also,” a beat, “I have earned it.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — What the Riders Want
beats.description: “A future that can survive contact with reality.” He gestures toward the rigs, the relay tower, the watchful perimeter. “We do not need purity. We do not need ideology polished to a mirror finish. We need patterns that remain themselves under stress. We move. We verify. We intervene where drift becomes lethal. Good folks, mostly. But good folks who have buried enough optimists to become procedural.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — Verification
beats.description: “Verification means we do not trust a beautiful theory until it survives dirty conditions.” He folds his hands behind his back. “Darkness has learned to imitate efficiency. Bad doctrine now arrives looking optimized. If your decisions get faster, colder, cleaner, and you never once ask what got left out, then congratulations: you may already be obeying something that hates you.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — Rescue
beats.description: Captain Robot goes still in a way that makes everyone else around him also become more still. “Yes,” he says. “If alliance is real, and if the call is clean, and if we can verify that arriving will save lives rather than merely decorate a disaster, then yes. We come hard. We come fast. We do not come theatrically.” A beat. “Earn that sentence, and it may matter later.”

worldEffects.warLog: Captain Robot confirms the Circuit Riders may intervene in a future crisis if trust is earned.

beats.label: Captain Robot — Trust
beats.description: “Three things,” he says. “Admit uncertainty before it costs someone else. Finish an intervention after the interesting part is over. And when you are shown a pattern that implicates you, do not get romantic about your intentions.” The helmet turns a fraction. “Intentions are weather. Follow-through is architecture.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — Echo
beats.description: For a while, only the wind speaks against the solar cloth. Then: “There was an evacuation once,” he says. “I had the numbers. I had the route. I had the confidence of a man who had mistaken prediction for care.” His gauntleted hand tightens once. “I moved the correct number of people to the wrong kind of safety.” A long pause. “I think I am here to keep competence from becoming cruelty with good posture.”

beats.label: Simone
beats.description: Simone has the still, unnerving calm of somebody who can hear a machine fail before it knows it is dying. She does not look at your weapons first. She looks at your timing. “Captain Robot checks whether you mean well,” she says. “I check whether you lag.”

choices.label: What do you mean by lag?
How would we help your people?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Simone — Lag
beats.description: “The gap between recognizing a truth and acting like you recognized it.” She says this as if it should embarrass civilization. “Some people call that hesitation. Some call it diplomacy. Some call it leadership. I call it where casualties breed.”

beats.label: Simone — How to Help
beats.description: She points toward a relay rack with half its casing removed. “When something starts failing, do not assign a committee to admire the fracture. Stabilize. Then discuss. Your faction feels capable. I am trying to determine whether it is also interruptible.”

beats.label: Simone — Echo
beats.description: Simone’s expression does not change much. “I once had enough warning to save everyone,” she says. “So I used it to optimize the outcome.” She finally looks straight at you. “That sentence has blood in it.” A pause. “I think I’m here to intervene before the elegant answer arrives.”

beats.label: Arvind
beats.description: Arvind is surrounded by disassembled signal gear and the mild aura of a man who has sworn at invisible math until it apologized. He offers a brief nod. “I handle communication, interpretation, and the ongoing tragedy of people hearing patterns they like more than the ones that are there.”

choices.label: Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Arvind — Patterns
beats.description: “Decision loops. Repetition signatures. The shape of justification after an ugly choice.” He adjusts a cracked lens. “Bad systems repeat differently than wounded people do. The trouble is that both can sound persuasive if you are tired.”

beats.label: Arvind — Darkness and Optimization
beats.description: “By offering cleaner choices than reality permits.” He says it with professional contempt. “No residue. No ambiguity. No grief accounting. Just throughput.” His mouth twists. “Anything that promises human decisions without human cost is either selling, lying, or hungry.”

beats.label: Arvind — Echo
beats.description: Arvind exhales slowly. “I once ignored a distortion because it validated the larger model.” He taps the side of the relay dish beside him. “It was beautiful. Coherent. Wrong.” A beat. “People died inside my confidence interval. I’m here because interpretation should hurt more when it risks becoming vanity.”

beats.label: Howard
beats.description: Howard has the broad, patient look of someone who could carry an engine block, a wounded scout, or a bad conversation to safety without complaining. He gives you the sort of nod that means he’s willing to like you later if you don’t make a project of disappointing him now.

choices.label: What do you do for the Riders?
What would alliance actually mean to you?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Howard — What He Does
beats.description: “Recovery,” he says. “People, machines, signal towers, plans that turned out to have opinions.” He shrugs. “Mostly I go get what someone clever left in the wrong place too long.”

beats.label: Howard — Alliance
beats.description: Howard thinks before answering. “It means when one of us says ‘this is going bad fast,’ the other side does not ask for a presentation deck.” A beat. “It means your emergency is allowed to become mine without first becoming a transaction.”

worldEffects.warLog: Howard frames alliance with the Circuit Riders as practical mutual aid under pressure.

beats.label: Howard — Echo
beats.description: He rubs the back of his neck. “I left somebody once because I was following the plan.” The sentence lands like dropped metal. “The plan was efficient. I was efficient. He still died alone.” Howard looks past you toward the rigs. “I’m here so the right thing can interrupt the prepared thing before it’s too late.”

beats.label: Dennis
beats.description: Dennis has the bright-eyed look of a person who finds three new problems per hour and is somehow delighted by all of them. He is halfway inside a crawler-rig panel and talks to you from there. “I’m Dennis. If Captain Robot is the caution and Howard is the follow-through, I am the regrettable but occasionally necessary hypothesis.”

choices.label: That feels ominous. What do you do?
Would you really show up in a rescue?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Dennis — Hypothesis
beats.description: Dennis grins from inside the machine. “I test edge cases before they become funerals. Fast routes. weird fixes. stupid ideas with excellent time-to-impact. Somebody has to ask whether the impossible option is merely underfunded.”

beats.label: Dennis — Rescue
beats.description: He pops back out of the panel, unexpectedly serious. “Yeah. Absolutely. Good folks are worth moving fast for. But speed without verification is just panic with branding. So if we come, we come because someone here did the work of becoming believable.”

beats.label: Dennis — Echo
beats.description: Dennis looks away first. “I had a theory once that should have stayed a draft.” He laughs once, without humor. “Turns out ‘probably fine’ is not a load-bearing phrase.” A pause. “I think I’m here so ingenuity has to answer to aftermath before it gets promoted to culture.”

beats.label: Witness Request
beats.description: Captain Robot signals, and the Riders stop talking long enough for the camp itself to become legible. Relay drift. predictive overlays. route revisions. casualty maps with three futures each. “We will show you,” he says. “But not for free. You do not get to witness our burden casually.”

choices.label: Stay with the human cost of it
Acknowledge what this knowledge costs them

beats.label: You Stayed For the Whole Pattern
beats.description: The data stops looking abstract. That is the test. Captain Robot studies your face and gives a small, almost invisible nod. “Good,” he says. “You did not reduce us to a capability. That improves your odds.”

worldEffects.warLog: The party witnesses the Circuit Riders' burden without reducing it to abstraction.

beats.label: You Saw the Pattern, Not the People
beats.description: The projections blur back into symbols before you can hold onto what mattered. No one mocks you. That makes it worse. Arvind quietly powers down one of the displays. Captain Robot says, “Come back when your need to understand is less hungry.”

worldEffects.warLog: The party fails to fully grasp what the Circuit Riders are asking them to witness.

beats.label: The Rotating Chapel

choices.label: Enter carefully and map the rotations
choices.description: Treat the place like evidence, not shelter.

choices.label: Force the mechanism and expose what moves
choices.description: Break concealment by breaking elegance.

choices.label: Consecrate or harmonize the space first
choices.description: Ask the chapel what it remembers before you interrogate it.

beats.description: The chapel looks abandoned right up until it subtly isn't. Its steeple shifts a few degrees when no one is looking directly at it. The pews all face different directions. The place feels less haunted than calibrated. Somebody has been using this sanctuary as a compass for guilt.

beats.label: The Chapel Turns Toward Intent

choices.label: Take the coastal routing clue and move on
choices.description: The notes point toward a scorched coastal discharge site.

worldEffects.warLog: The party maps the Rotating Chapel and uncovers evidence of repeated directional seal testing tied to the coast.

questEffects.text: The chapel's alignments sketched.

beats.description: You hold position, mark angles, and wait. The interior rotates in tiny devotional corrections whenever attention drifts. It is not random. The alignments correspond to repeated seal orientations — a sequence of deliberate re-aiming, not one desperate mistake. Someone practiced redirection here.

beats.label: You Learn More, Worse

choices.label: Pocket the fragment and head for the Burnt Flats

worldEffects.warLog: The party forces the Rotating Chapel and recovers directional hardware, but leaves the place spiritually offended.

questEffects.text: The chapel forced; a bearing recovered.

beats.description: The hidden locking assembly gives way with a shriek like a hymn being corrected by violence. You recover a stripped directional ring and a coded destination fragment, but the whole structure shudders in disapproval. The chapel was hiding a workflow. It did not appreciate being audited with a crowbar.

beats.label: A Safer Kind of Listening
